newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli stock market continues to surge.
newsitem.headline: Israeli stock market continues to surge.

text.p: Israeli shares rose on Tuesday for the fifth straight session with activity at its highest level in three years, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares climbed 1.84 percent, or 4.14 points, to 229.15 on a high all-share turnover of 194 million shekels against 156 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.88 percent higher at 237.12.

"The market continued to show strength today despite the fact that traders expected a technical correction. Towards the end of the trading day we saw some profit-taking and this might continue tomorrow," said Danniella Finn at Batucha Securities and Investments.

"The market's strength is very surprising. The main reason for the recent rise is that new money comes into the market through the provident and mutual funds," Finn said. "Today's rise was also a reaction to the rise of Israeli shares traded in New York."
Official figures showed that provident funds registered net accruals of 397.4 million shekels in December, marking the first time in 1996 they enjoyed a net inflow of money.

"Activity rose sharply and the turnover is the highest we have seen for a very long time. New money comes into the market and local investors show more interest in it," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeler Eblagon Securities.
"The session opened with a sharp rise of around three percent but by mid-day the indices started falling because of profit taking," Eidelheit added.
Elbit rose the maximum 10 percent to 757 after its shares traded on Nasdaq surged 23.3 percent on Monday.

Koor Industries, the second most active share, climbed 5.5 percent to 30,332 on volume of 8.8 million shekels. Traders said Koor gained after its New York share rose above its closing price on Monday in Tel Aviv.
The most active share was Bezeq Israel Telecom, which fell 1.0 percent to 821 on turnover of 10 million shekels.
Bank Leumi, the third most active, rose 2.75 percent to 490 on volume of 7.4 million shekels.
